summary.headline: Ramkrishna Forgings Q2 FY27 revenue rose 54.9% YoY to Rs 1,405 crore, with EBITDA margin at 18.23% and PAT of Rs 71 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached Rs 1,405 crore in Q2 FY27, up 54.9% YoY and 15.5% QoQ, with EBITDA (excluding other income) of Rs 256 crore and margin of 18.23% versus 13.5% a year ago and 17.96% in Q1. PBT was Rs 95 crore against a loss of Rs 10 crore last year, and PAT was Rs 71 crore, up 47% QoQ. Order wins of Rs 673 crore were booked, 52% from exports, with Rs 447 crore from castings, including a new North American light-vehicle casting programme. Management reiterated FY27 debt reduction of Rs 500 crore and ROCE of 12-15% by year-end, while declining to give FY28 guidance beyond a strong outlook for the next six months.

segments.commentary: Rs 7 crore EV orders and Rs 90 crore farm equipment orders in Q2.

segments.name: Casting
segments.commentary: Rs 447 crore of Q2 orders; casting utilisation reportedly about 88%, with aluminium and cold forgings running above 50% utilisation.

segments.name: Railway wheels JV
segments.commentary: 300 wheels under railway inspection; first phase of 2,000-3,000 wheels per month targeted from December; 20,000-25,000 wheels expected in FY27; 18-20% EBITDA margin at optimum utilisation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 total debt reduction of Rs 500 crore maintained; gross debt expected at about Rs 1,670-1,700 crore by year end.
FY27 group capex expected at about Rs 550 crore, with about Rs 160 crore in H2 mainly machining, plus Rs 15-20 crore JV investment in H2 and the balance next year.
FY28 debt reduction aim of Rs 300-400 crore; finance cost savings of about Rs 40 crore per annum from repaying Rs 500 crore at about 8% interest.
FY27 ROCE expected at 12-15% by year end; 20% ROCE set as an aspiration for next year.
EBITDA margin expected to improve by 30-40 bps QoQ; management aims to return to previous peak margins without a timeline.
Management expects a strong H2 FY27 and a strong market for the next six months; no FY28 guidance until full-year results.
Rs 8 crore to Rs 9 crore net shipping cost impact in Q2 expected to persist if freight stays at current levels.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex about Rs 390 crore plus Rs 40 crore JV investment; FY27 capex now guided at about Rs 550 crore versus Rs 350 crore guided in Q1.

Railway wheels JV: first-phase 140,000 wheels and second-phase 140,000 wheels; project cost Rs 2,180 crore; Rs 56 crore approval sought for phase 2; remaining JV equity about Rs 50-55 crore to be paid over next year.
Aluminium forging capacity about 3,000 tonnes; aluminium and cold forging utilisation above 50%.
Casting business at about 88% utilisation per analyst; management says capacity is sufficient for the new orders, with any capex planned for next year.
Wheels JV: 80% of capacity targeted in Q4 FY27 for 4,000-5,000 wheels per month.
demand_pricing: Q2 orders Rs 673 crore: 48% domestic, 52% export; Rs 447 crore casting, of which Rs 272 crore North American LV casting for a new customer and new product.
Geographic mix: North America about 58% and Europe about 41% of export revenue, versus Europe about 28% two years ago.
Lead time from order to delivery averages 6 months; exports 9-12 months and domestic 3-4 months.

Steel price pass-through is achieved in domestic market; North American and European contracts did not pass through the Indian steel increase, and Rs 6-7 crore raw material negative carry was absorbed in Q2.
Management expects another domestic steel price hike possibly in January and says it is prepared to pass it on.
Management said shipping rates have largely settled at peak, with no incremental increase seen currently.

qa_highlights.question: When will the Rs 447 crore casting orders be executed and is there capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: North American LV casting needs 6-9 months of validation after sample development; domestic casting starts within 12-14 weeks of development. Management said there is enough capacity for now.

qa_highlights.question: Why has FY27 capex risen and how much is left?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided about Rs 550 crore for FY27 across the group, mainly machining and value-add capacity; JV capex of about Rs 50-55 crore is pending over the next year.

qa_highlights.question: Gross debt at year end?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt at March 2026 was Rs 2,173 crore; year-end FY27 gross debt is expected at about Rs 1,670-1,700 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Power and shipping cost trends and margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Power cost fell on lower surcharges; other expenses rose on shipping costs, which will ease only when freight falls. Management expects 30-50 bps margin expansion every quarter and aims to return to previous peak margins without a timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Was there inventory gain in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: No inventory gain; there was a negative carry of about Rs 6-7 crore on raw material price increases in exports.

qa_highlights.question: Europe revenue appears flat YoY; why?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity was reallocated to North America, which recovered sharply; the Europe dip is marginal and expected to be recovered next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Shipping cost impact in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Net unrecovered shipping cost impact was about Rs 8-9 crore in Q2; part of the increase has been passed to customers.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Net working capital rose about Rs 140 crore on volume growth, with receivable and inventory days near March levels; shipping delays kept shipments in inventory, and management expects improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Did the company give FY28 or FY29 revenue targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify FY28 growth or revise margin trajectory; Lalit Khetan confirmed an aspiration of Rs 8,000 crore revenue for FY29 but said timing would be updated later. Management said guidance will come after full-year results.

risks_watch: Shipping costs and geopolitical tensions: Rs 8-9 crore quarterly unrecovered freight, and management said some cost will be borne if freight stays high.
Working capital: net working capital up about Rs 140 crore in H1 on higher receivables and inventory from delayed export shipments.
Railway wheels JV: commercial production and RDSO/railway inspection timing, plus funding and the Rs 56 crore phase-2 approval; JV first-year depreciation and interest impact not quantified.
Consolidated margin dilution as casting (lower margin than forgings) scales; management said this may keep consolidated margins somewhat muted.
Europe export revenue flat YoY in Q2, with FTA ratification timing uncertain and no inquiries yet from UK FTA.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, order flow and near-term utilisation, but guarded on specifics: management repeatedly declined to give FY28 guidance, margin timelines or customer-level detail, and gave only six-month visibility.
key_quotes: We believe that high utilization of our existing capaci ty and improved product mix and continued operating discipline will support growth and profitability in the coming quarters.

We would like to not comment on what is going to happen in FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Casting utilisation at ~88% and aluminium/cold forging above 50%; management says casting capacity is sufficient for current orders with any casting capex planned for next year, and phase-2 JV approval of Rs 56 crore is sought.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects a strong H2 FY27 and strong market for six months, with Q2 revenue up 54.9% YoY, but has declined to raise or quantify beyond the existing guide.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Rs 8-9 crore quarterly net shipping cost and Rs 6-7 crore raw material negative carry in North America/Europe contracts persist if freight stays high, and net working capital rose ~Rs 140 crore in H1.

rows.label: New product launch

rows.label: Rs 500 crore FY27 debt reduction
rows.why: Debt reduction of Rs 126 crore achieved in H1 FY27 and gross debt guided to fall from Rs 2,173 crore to about Rs 1,670-1,700 crore, with ~Rs 40 crore annual finance cost saving from repaying Rs 500 crore at ~8%.

rows.label: Rs 673 crore Q2 order wins, 52% export
rows.why: Q2 orders of Rs 673 crore (CV Rs 304 crore, LV Rs 272 crore, casting Rs 447 crore) with 6-month average order-to-delivery lead time convert into revenue in the window; exports take 9-12 months.

rows.label: Domestic steel price pass-through and possible January hike
rows.why: Steel price pass-through is achieved in the domestic market and management expects another steel hike possibly in January and is prepared to pass it on, while North American and European contracts did not pass through the Indian steel increase.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, order flow, the railway wheels JV ramp and margin direction, but cautious on FY28 guidance, margin timelines and customer detail; analysts pushed on capacity, capex and shipping cost impact.
